business_problem: Rabbit needed to operate hundreds of isolated enterprise tenants and run large-scale cost optimization analytics without building an operations-heavy platform, because its small engineering team had to scale FinOps automation safely and cheaply.
solution_summary: Rabbit built its cloud-optimization platform on a fully managed Google Cloud architecture so a small team could manage hundreds of isolated enterprise tenants without maintaining a large operations function. Cloud Run hosts the core services and scales to zero when idle, Google Kubernetes Engine orchestrates heavier data-collection pipelines, and Cloud SQL plus Firestore handle tenant orchestration and operational state. At the center of the analytics layer, BigQuery powers real-time cost analysis and counterfactual pricing simulations over more than 10 billion jobs and more than 500 petabytes of storage metadata. Supporting services such as Memorystore for Redis, Pub/Sub, Cloud Scheduler, Secret Manager, Cloud Build, Cloud Logging, and Cloud Monitoring round out the platform's eventing, secrets, deployment, and observability stack. This design lets Rabbit turn a stable serverless foundation into a FinOps product that actively manages capacity and automates cost savings.

data_flow: Tenant usage and metadata are collected through GKE-based pipelines, routed through event-driven services into Cloud Run-hosted application logic, stored in operational databases, and analyzed in BigQuery so Rabbit can simulate pricing, adjust reservations, and push automated cost optimizations safely across isolated customer environments.
business_outcome: Rabbit helped Lufthansa cut total BigQuery costs by 52%, helped Daangn cut monthly spend by 41%, and uses the same serverless architecture to optimize hundreds of enterprise tenants and monitor over 500 PB of BigQuery storage data.
